new_entities.name: Eccentric-emphasised training
new_entities.description: Training that emphasizes the eccentric phase of movement to increase mechanical loading on the muscle-tendon unit.

new_entities.name: Athletic tendon stiffness
new_entities.description: The mechanical stiffness of tendons relevant to force transmission and athletic performance.

edges.effect_quant: A 2022 meta-analysis of 61 articles and 763 participants found that mechanical loading increases lower-limb tendon stiffness overall (SMD 0.74, 95% CI 0.62 to 0.86), with higher-strain resistance protocols showing the strongest effects (SMD 1.04, 95% CI 0.65 to 1.43). But eccentric-emphasised trials are not uniformly positive: high-load eccentric knee-extensor training improved patellar tendon force, stiffness, and modulus at high torque levels, whereas accentuated eccentric loading in already-trained men did not change patellar tendon stiffness over 10 weeks.
edges.population: healthy athletes and trained adults using eccentric-emphasised loading to drive tendon adaptation
edges.mechanism: Eccentric-emphasised loading can expose the tendon to high strains that encourage mechanical adaptation, but the response depends heavily on baseline training status and whether the protocol meaningfully exceeds habitual loading.
edges.summary: The broader tendon-loading literature is clearly supportive, but the eccentric-specific athlete signal is less tidy than the hype suggests. Eccentric-emphasised work can help tendon stiffness, yet it is not guaranteed to outperform other heavy loading strategies in already-trained populations.
edges.caveats: This edge is especially sensitive to population and protocol. Untrained or rehab populations may respond differently from already-trained athletes, and some studies show little extra tendon benefit from accentuated eccentric loading once a high-strength baseline is already present.

evidence.notes: Mechanical, Material and Morphological Adaptations of Healthy Lower Limb Tendons to Mechanical Loading: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

evidence.citation: WalkerS et al 2020 Eur J Appl Physiol
evidence.notes: Increased fascicle length but not patellar tendon stiffness after accentuated eccentric-load strength training in already-trained men.

evidence.citation: MahieuNN et al 2008 Med Sci Sports Exerc
evidence.notes: Effect of eccentric training on the plantar flexor muscle-tendon tissue properties.
